name: Stock board, 4 cores
blurb: What your gateway came with. Runs three programs at once.

name: Varga V8 processor
blurb: Eight cores pulled from a decommissioned render farm. Programs run half again as fast, four at once.

name: Varga V16 processor
blurb: Sixteen cores. A password that took a minute takes thirty seconds. Five programs at once.

name: Kessel quantum co-processor
blurb: Nobody at the Backroom will say where these come from. Programs run three times as fast, six at once.

name: Varga V32 workstation board
blurb: Thirty-two cores in a case that hums. Programs run three and a half times as fast, six at once.

name: Kessel Q2 co-processor
blurb: The second generation of the quantum card the Backroom does not talk about. Programs run four times as fast and a little more, seven at once.

name: Orsted lattice array
blurb: A rack of lattice chips built for a weather office. Programs run five times as fast, seven at once.

name: Kessel Q4 cluster
blurb: Four quantum cards on one bus. Programs run six times as fast, eight at once.

name: Hadley photonic core
blurb: Light instead of current. Nobody sells it; somebody always has one. Programs run seven and a half times as fast, eight at once.

name: Null-grade processor stack
blurb: Hardware that should not be for sale to anyone. Programs run nine times as fast, nine at once.

name: Stock drive, 40 GB
blurb: What your gateway came with.

name: Solid-state array, 80 GB
blurb: Twice the room for programs and the files you bring home.

name: Solid-state array, 160 GB
blurb: Room for every program on the market and a good haul of files.

name: Cold-storage rack, 320 GB
blurb: Enough to host a large model and still bring home whole archives.

name: Cold-storage rack, 480 GB
blurb: A rack and a half of cold storage. Room for a library of programs and the archives you bring home.

name: Cold-storage rack, 640 GB
blurb: More room than any one job will ever need, until the next one.

name: Archive vault, 960 GB
blurb: Almost a terabyte, in a case that used to sit in a records office.

name: Archive vault, 1.3 TB
blurb: Room to keep everything you have ever copied, and every program you have ever built.

name: Tape library, 2 TB
blurb: Slow to look at, enormous to live with. Room for whole companies.

name: Data lake, 3 TB
blurb: A rented slice of a data centre, wired into your gateway under a shell company. Room for anything.

name: Stock modem
blurb: What your gateway came with.

name: Bonded line, 2 channels
blurb: Two lines bonded into one. Files copy and delete half again as fast.

name: Bonded line, 4 channels
blurb: Files copy and delete twice as fast. Less time with the firewall open.

name: Leased fibre
blurb: A line rented under a shell company's name. Files move three times as fast.

name: Leased fibre, dual
blurb: Two fibre lines under two shell companies. Files move three and a half times as fast.

name: Leased fibre, quad
blurb: Four fibres. Files move four and a half times as fast.

name: Backbone tap
blurb: A quiet tap on a regional backbone. Files move six times as fast.

name: Exchange-point port
blurb: A port inside an internet exchange. Files move eight times as fast.

name: Submarine splice
blurb: A splice on a trans-oceanic cable that is not on any map. Files move eleven times as fast.

name: Single port
blurb: What your gateway came with. One connection at a time.

name: Dual-port card
blurb: Hold two connections open at once, each through its own route, each with its own trace.

name: Quad-port card
blurb: Three connections at once. Keep one server busy while you work on another.

name: Octa-port card
blurb: Four connections at once, each with its own route and its own trace.

name: Switching fabric
blurb: Five connections at once. Run a whole job across several servers without hanging up.

name: Patch-panel cabinet
blurb: Six connections at once. It looks like something that belongs in an office.

name: Inference card
blurb: Runs Magpie 8B on your own gateway, for good. No rent, no farm. The weights take 8 GB of storage.

name: Inference cluster
blurb: Runs Heron 120B on your own gateway, for good. The weights take 30 GB of storage.

name: Trace sensor
blurb: Reads a trace closing in on your gateway and times it to the second, with no Trace Tracker program to run or store.

name: Heat-sink kit
blurb: Fins and a fan. The processor holds its top speed for longer, so programs run a tenth faster.

name: Liquid loop
blurb: A closed water loop. Programs run a fifth faster than the processor alone allows.

name: Chilled loop
blurb: A loop that runs off a small compressor. Programs run a third faster again.

name: Immersion tank
blurb: The board sits in oil. Programs run half again as fast as the processor alone allows.

name: Cryo plate
blurb: A plate that sits at minus forty. Programs run seventy percent faster.

name: Cascade chiller
blurb: A cascade of compressors in a case the size of a bin. Programs run twice as fast as the processor alone allows.
